title: Finite-type morphisms are stable under composition and base change
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $h:Y\to Z$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Finite type means locally of finite type and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. (1) If $f$ and $h$ are of finite type, then $h\circ f:X\to Z$ is of finite type. (2) If $f$ is of finite type and $a:Y'\to Y$ is any scheme morphism, then the projection $X\times_Y Y'\to Y'$ from the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] is of finite type. No separatedness, Noetherian, or finiteness hypothesis on $a$ is imposed.
